_comment: Frozen cross-implementation golden vectors for the Warren tunnel handshake (postcard). Every language SDK must reproduce these bytes. Any change is a wire break and requires bumping PROTOCOL_VERSION.

setup._comment: postcard layout (v6): protocol_version u8, features u32 varint, connection_index u8, total_connections u8, daita_support bool, device_id [u8;16] raw, client_pubkey [u8;32] raw, auth_sig [u8;64] raw (no length prefixes). v5 moved client auth off the TLS layer: client_pubkey is the client's Ed25519 identity and auth_sig signs 'warrenguard/inband-auth/v1' || channel_binding(32) || device_id(16). The signature is connection-bound (depends on the live TLS exporter), so it is NOT part of a frozen vector; these vectors pin the byte LAYOUT only, using fixed filler bytes for client_pubkey/auth_sig.

setup_ack._comment: postcard layout: protocol_version u8, tunnel_ipv4 [u8;4], tunnel_ipv6 Option (0x00 None / 0x01 + 16 bytes Some), exit_pubkey [u8;32], max_mtu u16 varint, multiconn_attached bool, daita_spec Option (0x00 None). Unchanged in v5 except protocol_version (5). v6 (wg-0005) appends exit_auth_sig [u8;64] raw: the exit's Ed25519 signature over 'warrenguard/inband-server-auth/v1' || channel_binding(32). Connection-bound, so this vector pins the byte LAYOUT only, using fixed filler bytes.

vectors._comment: daita_spec Some: 0x01, then DaitaConfig: machine_specs Vec<String> (len varint + per-string len varint + utf8), max_padding_frac f64 (8 bytes LE IEEE-754), max_blocking_frac f64. Pins the f64 byte order across languages.
